mainTopic: Rocks inside a field being sold, the new משנה on selling land 'measured with a rope' versus 'more or less', and the גמרא's question about a plain 'בית כור'
overview: This amud first finishes the discussion about rocks in a field sold as a בית כור. The גמרא asks whether the shape of the rocks matters (a ring, a row, an angle, a crooked path), and each question ends in תיקו. A ברייתא teaches that a lone rock, or a rock next to the border, is never measured with the field. רב פפא and רב אשי ask follow-up questions about earth between the rock and the border, and about layers of earth and rock, and these also end in תיקו. Then a new משנה begins. If the seller promised a בית כור 'measured with a rope', any difference must be corrected. If he said 'more or less', a difference of up to a רובע per סאה is allowed. Extra land is normally paid back with money to protect the seller, but a piece big enough to be its own plot is returned as land, and once payback is owed, all the extra is returned. The גמרא then asks what the law is when the seller just said 'a בית כור', and starts a proof from the משנה's wording that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Questions about how the rocks are arranged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is when the rocks in the field form a ring, a row, an angle or a crooked path. It leaves all of these questions unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the rocks are arranged like a ring, what is the law? In a row? Forming an angle? In a crooked path? These questions stay unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks four quick questions about the shape the rocks form in the field. It cannot answer them, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion was about whether rocks spread over a field count as part of the field's measurement. Here the גמרא asks whether the shape of the rock arrangement changes that law. No answer is found, so each question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Forming an angle or corner shape
'Let it stand': the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the law is one way or the other. It means the גמרא could not decide, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: If the rocks are arranged like a ring, what is the law?
If they stand in a row, what is the law?
If they form an angle, what is the law?
If they form a crooked path, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about rocks in a field sold as a בית כור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the shape of the rock arrangement (ring, row, angle, crooked path) change whether the rocks are measured with the field?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. All the questions are left as תיקו.

steps.title: A lone rock or a rock by the border is not measured
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a single rock, even a small one, is not measured with the field. The same is true of a rock next to the field's border.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if there was a single lone rock, even a tiny one, it is not measured together with the field. And if the rock was right next to the border, even a tiny one, it is not measured together with the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with two clear rules about rocks that are left out of the field's measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lone rock is not counted as part of the field, no matter how small it is. The same applies to a rock touching the edge of the field. The size does not matter in either case.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even the smallest
It is not measured together with the field
The border or boundary of the field

phrases.english: It was taught: If there was a solitary rock,
even if it is of minimal size,
it is not measured together with the field.
And if it was adjacent to the border,
even if it is of minimal size,
it is not measured together with the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the unresolved questions, a ברייתא gives two settled cases about rocks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lone rock, or a rock next to the border, is never measured as part of the field, even if it is tiny.

steps.title: What if some earth separates the rock from the border?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether a rock still counts as being next to the border if a strip of earth separates them. The question is left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if there is earth separating the rock from the border, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks about the ברייתא's second rule: what if the rock is near the border but some earth separates it from the border?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said a rock next to the border is not measured. רב פפא asks whether a little earth in between means the rock no longer counts as next to the border. The question is not decided.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If earth separates them in between, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the rock and the field's border from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: מוּפְסָק עָפָר בֵּינְתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the ברייתא's rule about a rock 'next to the border' reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a rock separated from the border by earth still count as 'next to the border'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question is left as תיקו.

steps.title: What about layers of earth and rock?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about earth below with rock on top, or earth on top with rock below. This question is also left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if there is earth below and rock above, or earth above and rock below, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question about land where earth and rock are layered one on top of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether layered ground counts as usable earth or as rock when measuring the field. He gives both versions: rock covering earth, and earth covering rock. No answer is found.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
Earth below and rock above;
earth above and rock below: what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: All of the questions about rock shapes, a gap of earth, and layers end in תיקו. Only the ברייתא's two rules (a lone rock, and a rock touching the border, are not measured) are settled.
steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: עָפָר מִלְּמַטָּה וְצוּנְמָא לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another follow-up question about rocks, this time about layers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When earth and rock are layered, is the area counted as earth or as rock for measuring?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer. The question is left as תיקו.

steps.title: משנה: Land sold 'measured with a rope' must be exact
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that if a seller promises a בית כור 'measured with a rope', any shortage or extra, however small, must be paid back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says, 'I am selling you a בית כור of land, measured with a rope': if he gave even a tiny bit less, the seller must take that off the price. If he gave even a tiny bit more, the buyer must give it back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the rule for a sale where the seller promised an exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'measured with a rope' makes the deal precise. Because of that, any difference either way must be corrected. A shortage means the seller returns money, and for extra land the buyer must make it up to the seller (step 7 explains how).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of the משנה)
An area of land big enough to plant a כור of seed
Measured with a rope, meaning measured exactly
He must deduct from the price

phrases.english: MISHNA:
'I am selling you a beit kor of earth,
measured with a rope,'
if he gave even slightly less, he deducts it from the price;
if he gave even slightly more, it must be returned.
phrases.notes: The buyer has to make up the extra to the seller. Step 7 explains this is usually done with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ מִדָּה בְּחֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about how exact the measurement in a land sale must be.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the land is sold 'measured with a rope', any difference, even a tiny one, must be corrected.

steps.title: משנה: Land sold 'more or less' allows a small margin
steps.stepSummary: If the seller said 'more or less', a difference of up to a רובע per סאה (one twenty-fourth) is allowed. Anything beyond that must be settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'more or less', then even if he gave a רובע per סאה less, or a רובע per סאה more, it belongs to him. If the difference is more than that, they must make a calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case: the seller said 'more or less', and this allows a small margin of difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'More or less' tells the buyer not to expect an exact amount. So a difference of up to a רובע (a quarter קב) for each סאה, which is one twenty-fourth, needs no correction. Beyond that margin, they work out the difference and the side that lost out is paid back.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether less or more ('more or less')
A quarter קב per סאה, which is one twenty-fourth
It is his, it has reached him (no correction needed)
He must make a calculation and settle up

steps.confusionAlert: 'More or less' does not mean any difference is fine. Only up to one twenty-fourth is allowed. Beyond that, the difference must be settled.

phrases.english: And if he said: 'Whether less or more,'
even if he gave a quarter per se'a less,
phrases.notes: A סאה is six קב, so a quarter קב per סאה works out to one twenty-fourth.

phrases.english: or he gave a quarter per se'a more,
it is his.
More than this, he must make a calculation.

steps.whatToRemember: 'Measured with a rope' means exact, so every difference is corrected. 'More or less' allows a margin of one twenty-fourth, and anything beyond that is settled.
steps.whyThisMatters: The exact wording of a sale decides how strict the measurement is. The גמרא will go on to discuss these two expressions.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר: הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting case to step 5: a loose measurement instead of an exact one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 'more or less', a difference of up to a רובע per סאה needs no correction; a bigger difference must be calculated and settled.

steps.title: The buyer pays back the extra with money, or with land if the seller wants
steps.stepSummary: When the buyer received too much land, he pays the seller money for the extra. If the seller prefers, the buyer gives back the extra land instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the buyer give back to the seller? Money. And if the seller wants, the buyer gives him back land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from step 6. It now tells us how the buyer settles up when he received more land than he paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal payback is money for the extra land. The seller has a choice, though: he can ask for the extra land back instead. So the choice belongs to the seller, not the buyer.

phrases.english: What does he return to him? Money.
phrases.notes: This is the buyer who got too much land, paying back the seller.

phrases.english: And if he wants, he returns land to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about extra land from steps 5 and 6. It now explains how the payback is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Extra land is paid back with money. If the seller wishes, the buyer returns the land itself.

steps.title: Money protects the seller, but a usable plot is returned as land
steps.stepSummary: The rule of paying money was made to strengthen the seller's position. But if the extra piece is big enough to stand as its own plot (nine קבין in a field, half a קב in a garden, or a רובע according to רבי עקיבא), the land itself is returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say he returns money? To strengthen the seller. Because if the extra left over in a field is an area of nine קבין, or in a garden an area of half a קב (or, according to רבי עקיבא, an area of a רובע), he returns the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains why money is the normal payback. It then gives the case where the land itself is given back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small leftover strip is useless on its own. So the seller is allowed to demand money for it instead of getting back a scrap of land. But when the extra piece is big enough to work as a field or garden by itself, the land itself goes back. רבי עקיבא gives a smaller size for a garden.

keyTerms.meaning: to strengthen his position, to give him the advantage
an area where nine קבין of seed are sown
an area where half a קב of seed is sown

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the money rule helps the buyer. It was made for the seller's benefit, so he is not stuck taking back a useless scrap of land.

phrases.english: And why did they say he returns money to him?
To strengthen the position of the seller –

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם שִׁיֵּיר בַּשָּׂדֶה בֵּית תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין,
phrases.english: for if there was left over in the field an area of nine kav,
phrases.notes: 'Left over' means the extra land the buyer got beyond what he paid for.

phrases.english: and in a garden an area of half a kav;
and according to the words of Rabbi Akiva – an area of a quarter-kav;
he returns the land to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for step 7's money rule and the case where land is returned instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money is the default so the seller is protected. An extra piece big enough to be its own plot is returned as land.

steps.title: Once payback is owed, all the extra is returned
steps.stepSummary: When the extra goes beyond the allowed margin, the buyer returns all of the extra, not just the part above the רובע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not return only the רובע. Rather, he returns all of the extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its section with one more rule about the 'more or less' sale from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a 'more or less' sale, a difference of up to a רובע per סאה is forgiven. You might think that once the difference is bigger, only the part above the margin is paid. The משנה says no: once any payback is owed, the whole extra is settled.
steps.whatToRemember: Extra land is paid back with money, unless the seller wants land. If the extra piece is a usable plot, the land itself goes back. And once payback is owed, all the extra is returned, not just the amount above the margin.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הָרוֹבַע בִּלְבַד הוּא מַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: And it is not only the quarter-kav that he returns,
rather, all of the extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אֶת הָרוֹבַע בִּלְבַד הוּא מַחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה by explaining how much is returned once the margin from step 6 is passed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the difference goes beyond the allowed margin, the entire extra must be settled.

steps.title: What if the seller just said 'a בית כור'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a seller who said only 'a בית כור', without adding 'measured with a rope' or 'more or less'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked of them: if he just said 'a בית כור', with no details, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It asks about a case the משנה did not spell out: a plain 'בית כור' with no extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two cases: exact ('measured with a rope') and loose ('more or less'). The question is which one a plain 'בית כור' counts as. Does it mean exact, so every small difference is paid back? Or loose, so a רובע per סאה is forgiven?

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked of them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
'A beit kor' without details, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a question about a case between the two cases in steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a plain 'בית כור' is treated as an exact sale or as a 'more or less' sale.

steps.title: Starting a proof from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to bring proof from the משנה's opening words: 'I am selling you a בית כור of earth, measured with a rope'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'I am selling you a בית כור of earth, measured with a rope'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה to prepare a proof for the question in step 10, and the argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to learn something from how the משנה is worded. The משנה's words 'measured with a rope' are being quoted so their meaning can be weighed against a plain 'בית כור'. The actual reasoning comes next.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'I am selling you a beit kor of earth –
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, see step 5.

phrases.english: measured with a rope',

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer step 10's question from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: How a plain 'בית כור' sale is treated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'בית כור עפר אני מוכר לך מדה בחבל'.
